finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can run purgeAll(). The sibling handler rotateKeys uses mustPerm and returns on failure, which shows the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated HTTP user with a User in the request context, with or without the admin permission, sending a request to the purge handler
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) gets the caller's user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored, so there is no branch and no early return

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (line 12) only returns u.Perms[perm] and writes no response. Only handlers.go exists, so there is no middleware or router in the repo that could enforce admin elsewhere. rotateKeys (line 33) does enforce the check correctly via mustPerm. userFrom (line 40) does an unchecked type assertion that panics if no user is in the context. That is a robustness issue, not an authorization bypass.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12) returns a bool only and is called as a bare statement at line 26. No middleware or router exists, since handlers.go is the only file. mustPerm (line 16) is the enforcing variant and is not used in purge.
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's bool result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys, which returns on a failed mustPerm at handlers.go:33-35.
